**[SUGGESTION]:** The Windows import allowlist accepts only `kernel32.dll`, so any future legitimate system import fails the release gate

`ws2_32.dll` (pulled in transitively the moment anything imports `net`) and `advapi32.dll` (`os/user`/registry on Windows) are OS-shipped system libraries that do not violate the self-contained-binary invariant this check enforces. Today's dependency set happens to import only `kernel32.dll`, but the first transitive `net`/`os/user` usage will make `inspectFormat` reject an otherwise correct build with the misleading `non-system Windows library: ws2_32.dll` error, forcing an allowlist edit under release pressure. Consider whitelisting the documented OS-shipped set (e.g. `kernel32.dll`, `ws2_32.dll`, `advapi32.dll`) — mirroring how the darwin branch already permits both `libSystem.B.dylib` and `libresolv.9.dylib` — or documenting the intentional strictness next to the check so the failure is diagnosable.
